missing.why: The verse calls Lot 'the son of Haran his son's son', so Terah is Lot's grandfather.
The verse calls Sarai Terah's 'daughter in law', Abram's wife, so Terah is her father-in-law.

note: No wrong rows: the Terah-Nahor-Serug-Reu-Peleg line and the Terah/Haran/Abram/Nahor-2 rows match the text, and the nahor (son of Serug) and nahor-2 (son of Terah) slugs are used correctly. The Sarai father-in-law row conflicts with 'sarai daughter-of terah' from GEN 20:12, a variant between books that is kept, not a wrong row here.
